quest.title: An Artist Adrift
quest.description: You find an artist from Fontaine in distress in a cave by the water...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x15000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should we leave it something nice to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Dog
dialogues.text: (Looks at you expectantly.)

talks.objective: Go to the camp by the water

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: I—I... *sigh* Thank you both for saving me.

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: I had a wonderful dream last night. In my dream, Caterpillar was standing at the end of the pilgrim's path, waving at me, and in that dream... Well, it was strange. Why was the path just one cavern after another?

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: But Caterpillar was there, standing at the very end of the narrow way, and so I ran toward him, but before I could reach him, the dog woke me up...

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: Leaving the part with the dog aside for the moment, I believed this to be a good omen, and so I brought my sketching tools and set out.

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: In the end... I wound up running through the maze like a headless Cicin, and I was even attacked by hilichurls... Not only did I not escape, but I also lost the bag containing my drafts during the chase...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess this is another day of losses for you.

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: But can you blame me? This place is even harder to navigate than the sewers in Fontaine! ...Wait, the people of Sumeru live in trees, right? Could this place really be...

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: What do the people of Sumeru even, um, excrete...!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This isn't what you're thinking about!

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: *sigh* My life has been but a series of failures. One ill-advised step after another.

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: Why did I leave my place of safety this morning? I saw a good omen in my dream, but it was just a dream, after all. Why did I take it for reality?

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: I should've been completely honest about the trouble I'm in... If I had asked you to lead the way, I wouldn't have ended up in this situation.

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: Oh, why did I leave Fontaine in the first place? My life there had not yet become untenable anyway... On the other hand, not a single good thing has occurred ever since I came here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't give up just yet! We can still take you to see some awesome places. But for now, we'll help you look for the things you've lost!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, even though we're not sure if we can get them back in one piece...

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: Haha, they might have been taken and used by hilichurls as toilet paper, for all we know! Well... Whatever the case... they weren't very expensive things anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Be honest, please.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. Even if they aren't worth much in terms of Mora, they're precious to you, aren't they? We'll help you find them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, where's Pepper? Isn't it with you?

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: Hmph, that heartless creature ran off a long time ago... It's probably relaxing in some hiding spot of its own right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's kinda hard to believe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, anyway, why don't you return to your camp first and treat your injuries? We'll come back and look for you once we find the lost items.

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: Thank you, my... friends. Ah, what have we to rely on in this life but friends?

talks.objective: Follow the path and look for the missing sketch

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Isn't this Pepper? It seems to be guarding something, too! Wait, this feels kinda familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Dog
dialogues.text: (It seems to have recognized you and wags its tail.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, is it guarding Julien's sketches?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Pepper barks twice before leaving quickly...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And there it goes again. It was like this the last time as well... Speaking of which, what do the hilichurls need sketches for?

choices.text: Perhaps they'd like some interior decorations.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, would they though...

choices.text: Perhaps they use it as toilet paper...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ugh! You have an awful imagination, {NICKNAME}!

talks.objective: Go to the camp and talk to Julien

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: As we thought, Pepper's already back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Julien! We found your sketches!

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: Ah, thank you so much, my friends... To think that you went through all that for such worthless items...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't say that! Aren't you a famous artist from Fontaine? Your sketches would sell for a pretty sum, wouldn't they?

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: Um, well, I suppose so... To be honest, I don't really think about things like that... True art should be priceless, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, no wonder you're a famous artist. Your words feel so full of... artistic flair! Speaking of which, Pepper was guarding your sketches when we found them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just like before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Paimon thinks that it still cares a lot about you.

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: You mean, that same dog who keeps leading me down strange paths no matter how long I've fed it, and leaves me to face the hilichurls on my own?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... I—It probably had some considerations of its own!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even though you're saying all these things, you actually really like Pepper, right? You wouldn't have taken a photo of it using a special Kamera otherwise.

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: Photo? What photo?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's a picture of a dog clipped between your sketches, and it looks just like Pepper. The colors used were quite unique too. You must have used some sort of special Kamera to take that photo, right?

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: Um... Actually, I drew that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? S—Seriously? Guess you're pretty good, Mr. Renowned Artist. Not only did it look very lifelike, but your use of colors was also very... um, artistic!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Did Paimon say anything wrong?)

choices.text: (Don't ask me. I don't get it either.)

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: I didn't want to draw like this... I just... wanted to become a first-rate artist. Do you also think it's an impossible endeavor?

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: *sigh* Sorry, I shouldn't have lied to you, my friends. Once you tell a lie, you have to keep on lying... I've had enough...

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: In truth, I'm just an amateur artist who can't "correctly" differentiate color the way other people do, but I didn't want to give up on my dream to become a true artist.

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: With the help of... a friend's powers, I am now able to draw anything exactly as it appears — but I still can't seem to tell colors apart.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you said that you can now draw anything exactly as it appears... Is that really something you can just... learn overnight?

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: Well, this friend of mine is quite a powerful person.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Really? That's kinda hard to believe.

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: Or perhaps I should say that I have lost my ability to draw things in a way other than exactly how it appears. I suppose this is what they call "the price of power." I know it sounds a little outrageous, but...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Julien replicates an Adventurer's Experience for you.\nYou study the replica and the original, and find no difference between them.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The only difference, perhaps, is that after you read it, the replica only leaves a strange, blank feeling in your mind...\nIt feels like you did read it, and yet you didn't. Like time alone was wasted without any experience gained...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It really doesn't look any different from the original...

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: Of course, I didn't become a famous artist of any sort, but I did become a real dab hand at counterfeiting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But isn't that illegal?

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: ...Exactly, and so after serving my sentence, I was determined to do something legitimate. This time, I will become a proper artist for sure!

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: But this ability to draw things in such exactitude... If Caterpillar had not been the one to grant it to me, I would have named it a curse.

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: I'm like a broken Kamera that can only create pictures with mismatched colors...

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: I believed that if I made a pilgrimage along the path of the Oceanids, I would be able to find a cure... that would let me differentiate color just like other people can, and grant me creativity akin to that of an innocent child...

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: A friend... a most reliable friend of mine. It was he who told me that following the path of the Oceanids' pilgrimage would allow me to find a curative in Sumeru that can cure all hurts and give one a new lease on life.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds super suspicious! What sort of friend is this again? ...Are you sure you didn't get tricked?

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: He has seen so much — why would he need to trick me? It must be my fault... Like I said before, my life is but a series of failures...

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: I guess this miracle cure must've been kept under tight lock and key, making it impossible for an ordinary man like me to find. I... I've already accepted that.

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: The dog probably didn't even want to come with me to Sumeru — it wouldn't have caused so much trouble otherwise. I should've just left it in Fontaine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon... thinks it definitely still wants to stay with you. It definitely loves your drawings as well... so c'mon, don't just give up like this!

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: Thank you for comforting me... But I've already given up hope. You've come to my aid several times now, and yet I haven't been able to repay you at all...

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: Once I have recovered, I will make preparations to return to Fontaine. This might seem like an impertinent request, but could you two guide me back to the main road?

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: *sigh* If I had given up earlier, or stopped trying to fool myself... perhaps I would already be on the right path.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if you just need us to guide you, that's fine. Since you've already made up your mind... let's wait until you're rested up!

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: Thank you, my friends.

choices.text: And what's this path of pilgrimage again?

response.speaker: Julien
response.text: Caterpillar told me that this is the path that the Oceanids took, and that the end of that path was Sumeru, where I'll find a cure that would heal anything and grant me a second chance at life...

choices.text: (Perhaps this is art beyond your comprehension, Paimon.)

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: The path of pilgrimage. How did I lose track of it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...The path of pilgrimage?

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: Ah, it's nothing. It's just... just a figure of speech.

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: Ah, my friends, the lost sketches...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We haven't gotten them yet.

dialogues.speaker: Julien
dialogues.text: I see. It's alright. They aren't valuable anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, isn't that Julien? He's surrounded! We've gotta go help him!
